report.summary: Recognizable, charming bank miniature: paired south gabled bays, pale siding, arched window groups, shallow rear roof, west drive-through canopy, and restrained east sign/window elevation read coherently. No obvious broken geometry is visible.

orientation.summary: The located SV1 camera is south of the building looking north and directly supports the +u face: it shows two distinct columned street-facing portals, matching the two +u double doors in the inventory and render—not an unsupported duplicated entrance. SV2’s north/northeast oblique view supports the single secondary -u parking-side door. SV4 shows the east (-v) window-and-sign elevation without a principal portal, matching the render; the west (+v) face appropriately carries the drive-through canopy and no door. Thus the door inventory—two +u, one -u, none on ±v—is source-consistent.

issues.problem: The oversized main hipped roof visually dominates the paired front gables more than in SV1, slightly weakening the characteristic shallow-roof silhouette.
issues.fix: Lower or visually flatten the main roof ridge while retaining the two prominent south gables.

scene_review.summary: The paired gabled front bays, pale siding, arched upper windows, long drive-through canopy, and regular signed elevation produce a recognizable, appealing Cary Bank & Trust. The main roof remains somewhat visually dominant, but this is a silhouette simplification rather than a defect; no broken faces or obvious repair failures are visible.

orientation.summary: The prior independent view identifies the two distinct +u/S street-facing portals, and the actual inventory contains one double door in each paired south bay. A third double door on -u/N matches the independently supported secondary parking-side entrance. There are no doors on the canopy or signed side faces, so the paired principal arrangement is supported rather than accidental duplication.
